extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers / novelists / storytellers seeking craft guidance
extracted.subtask_description: A method for writing fiction that centers the protagonist's internal struggle (misbelief → aha) and builds plot and scenes as causal, emotionally-driven manifestations of that inner change. Emphasizes neuroscience-informed tactics like emotion-first, anticipation, specificity, and rigorous backstory work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories Are About the Internal Struggle
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot is the external manifestation of the protagonist's internal struggle. The change inside is what readers feel. External action without internal change = events without story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus narrative energy on the protagonist's inner change; use external events to test and reveal that internal struggle rather than treating plot as an end in itself. Anti-pattern: a sequence of externally interesting events that don't produce an internal transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotion First, Always
rubrics_metrics.description: "Emotions engage the brain faster than anything else." Information without emotional valence doesn't stick. Quality fiction makes the reader feel before they think.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor scenes and opening pages in emotion so readers are viscerally engaged before intellectual comprehension follows. Use emotional stakes to make exposition and information memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Story Question (Scene-Level Wants and Obstacles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene must answer: what does the protagonist want, and what's keeping them from getting it? Internal stakes amplify external action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this question as a litmus test for each scene's purpose; ensure scenes present a clear want and obstacle that connect to the protagonist's internal agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: "Misbelief" — The Lie the Protagonist Believes
rubrics_metrics.description: The protagonist enters the story holding a false belief about themselves or the world that has shaped their life; the plot's events test that belief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a concrete misbelief as the motor of the internal arc; plan how plot events will interrogate and ultimately overturn it (the 'aha'). Note: some critics find this framework can over-determine character, so avoid making the misbelief feel contrived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause and Effect ("And So…")
rubrics_metrics.description: Every scene must connect to the next via 'and so' not 'and then.' The brain craves causality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct scenes so each one causally triggers the next, forming a logical chain rather than episodic events. Anti-pattern: loosely connected 'and then' sequences that feel aimless.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Backstory Counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Do deep work on the protagonist's backstory before drafting — not as info-dump but as the foundation for the misbelief and current behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use backstory to explain why the misbelief exists and to motivate present choices; integrate it into scenes through cause-effect rather than large expository passages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation Engages the Brain
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting up expectations (and meeting/subverting them) keeps readers engaged. 'What happens next?' is the brain's default mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create setups that provoke anticipation and then either meet or subvert expectations in ways that reveal character or deepen stakes. Use anticipation to sustain momentum across scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity Triggers Imagination
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic detail bores; specific detail lights up the brain's sensory cortices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concrete, sensory-specific details over vague description to engage readers' imaginations and make scenes memorable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Story Genius Process Steps
rubrics_metrics.description: A recommended sequence: 1) The 'What If' — initial story spark; 2) The 'Why' — protagonist's misbelief; 3) The 'Aha' — the truth they need; 4) Backstory development; 5) Plot built scene-by-scene around internal arc; 6) Each scene: cause / effect / realization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these steps as a scaffold for pre-drafting and plotting: generate premise, define misbelief and required realization, mine backstory for causal motivation, then craft scenes so each advances both plot and internal change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist's Want Clear by Page 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the reader know what the protagonist wants from page 1?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish the protagonist's want (external and/or internal) very early so readers are invested in the driving question. Use the first pages to orient desire and stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal Struggle Present (Quality Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there an internal struggle, not just external obstacles?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the narrative poses an inner problem that requires psychological change; if the work only piles on external problems without an internal arc, it may 'feel like nothing's happening.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene-level Causality (Quality Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does each scene cause the next?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 'and so' chain as a test for structural integrity: each scene's outcome should create the next scene's circumstances or choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Details Engage the Senses (Quality Test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do specific details engage the senses?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether descriptions use concrete sensory information to activate reader imagination; bland, generic prose is a fail on this metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending Pays Off the Misbelief→Aha Trajectory
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the ending pay off the misbelief→aha trajectory?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the resolution delivers the internal realization the story has been building toward and whether that internal change feels earned by the causal chain of events.
